confidence_notes: I based the food, coffee and beer anchors on web search results that collect typical prices. The main one was Expatica's summary of Numbeo data from June 2026: inexpensive meal about JPY 1,200, cappuccino about JPY 534, domestic 0.5 L draught beer about JPY 550 and three-course mid-range meal for two about JPY 7,010. Other cost-of-living sites gave similar figures, although their beer prices varied a lot, from about JPY 330 to 600. I set beer a little above the median because it is defined as a restaurant serving. I did not search for a JPY/USD rate. Yen prices were converted at an assumed rate of about JPY 150 per USD from my general knowledge, so all USD figures carry roughly 5-10% currency uncertainty. Cocktail and wine evidence was weak. One cross-city site guessed about JPY 2,082 per cocktail from very few data points, a 2026 nightlife guide gave JPY 1,000-2,000 as typical, and the only wine prices found were hotel-bar menus that are not representative. I set the cocktail at about JPY 1,300 and wine at about JPY 800 per glass. These figures are scaled from the local beer price and typical izakaya and casual restaurant pricing, so treat them as lower confidence. Accommodation anchors were not searched. They are general-knowledge estimates for July 2026, which is summer peak demand with recent hotel price inflation in Tokyo. Hotel prices vary widely by neighbourhood and date, so accommodation is the least certain group.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Tokyo's own aggregated cost-of-living data for food and drink. For accommodation, I compared Tokyo with other expensive, high-demand Asian cities such as Seoul and Singapore. My estimates put Tokyo's budget hotels and hostels above Seoul's and below Singapore's.
